title: PRICINGEXPERT — Kalshi Paper-Trading Competition & Research Desk
description: Autonomous live book-maker lab for prediction markets, focused on pricing theory rather than profit: it builds a public-data-only order-book model for Kalshi contracts (books, candles, schedules, settlements, market metadata, series and fees) and models the three things a bookmaker must decide — the fair price, the price to quote and the price at which to stop quoting. The model assumes an order-flow process whose initial estimate of the fair value is wrong, models the informed side as having observed the outcome while the uninformed side is noisy, states a pure market-maker objective of capturing the spread, and prices an American binary option by valuing the asset at exercise and converting to an event probability through the inverse CDF — the midpoint between the bid and the ask is a price, not an expectation. It publishes a scoring guide for spread captures (a continuous book with depth at every price scores a capture, a depleted or one-sided book scores a price change, a stale book scores no capture), a venue-analysis guide framed as mid-price precision and a mirror-fill cost, a 61-category research log with the explicit caveat that a category is a hypothesis class rather than a conclusion, and a stated limit that thin books inflate Kelly fractions and that public-data candles are not always printable. data/candles/ holds 84 committed candle files (53 KXBTC, 31 KXETHD) from 12 series, including every contract month under the KXBTCD and KXETHD series with official fetch provenance, and data/manifest.json's series-catalog entry is a 17,505,797-byte full series catalog with volume, sha256 af04b45aabd739cd0d3f78d782b327cdb72e7c23e6300e45566319d2da28. The competition has not traded: data/season-2026/forward/leaderboard.json reports cycles_completed 0 with 10 strategies all still at $10,000.00, realized_pnl 0.0 and 0 fills, and data/season-2026/forward/{trades,intents,marks}.jsonl are each 0 lines. scripts/verify.py was executed here and reports passed 1198, errors 0 (its checks array lists 12 V1/V2 messages phrased as the failures they did not find, so the string 'missing provenance' in that output means the opposite), and `python3 -m pytest tests -q` reports 39 passed. A new data/season-2026/backtest/results.json records a candle-replay backtest that states its own assumptions in the artifact: signal on bar t close, fill at bar t+1 open with no look-ahead, candle-proxied touches that are explicitly NOT book-verified, a default 2-cent limit buffer capped at 0.99, cumulative-volume gates and signed slippage.

flags: This entry was published as an empty placeholder and is now a 72-file research desk — the seventh stub-to-app reversal this directory has recorded (IRR-42, IRR-64, IRR-72, IRR-84, IRR-90 and now IRR-94), and the fastest: the snapshot that read it as one commit with a 15-byte README was generated at 01:37:24Z, three pull requests merged the whole project onto main at 02:25:30Z, 02:27:41Z and 02:28:34Z, and tools/audit_kind.py caught the reclassification about six minutes after that. Nothing was misreported at the time — main genuinely held only 'Initial commit' when it was read — but the published entry was true for 48 minutes.

Zero results, and that is stated rather than smoothed over: cycles_completed 0, 0 fills, 0 exits, 0 settlements, 0 captured books, 0 observations, and no backtest results file. A leaderboard of ten personas all sitting on exactly $10,000.00 is a season that has not started, not a competition with no winners. Every figure in this entry comes from the repository's own committed data files at a61a2eb.

The verification gate passes but is only half exercised, and the way it reports is a trap for a reader. `check(ok, code, msg)` in scripts/verify.py appends msg to CHECKS when ok is True and to ERRORS when it is False, and every msg is phrased as the failure it did not find — so the printed `passed: 42` sits next to lines reading 'V1: hash mismatch exchange-status.json' and 'V13-trades: duplicate rows detected', which look like 42 failures and are 42 passes. `errors: 0` with exit code 0 is the authoritative signal. V12 (link well-formedness) has no pass path at all — it calls check() only on a placeholder URL — so a clean link audit contributes nothing to either list, and remote reachability is CI-only via scripts/probe_links.py.

scripts/verify.py is not read-only: it writes data/site/link-audit.json as a side effect. Run in a clean clone it left `git status` empty, so the rewrite was byte-identical to the committed file — deterministic, and worth knowing before running it inside a working tree you care about.

The repository registers its own irregularities, in the same spirit as this directory: data/site/verification.json carries 3, recording that direct HTTPS from its build sandbox cannot reach api.elections.kalshi.com (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL on connect while DNS resolves), so evidence collection went through the platform's server-side fetch route with the tool used recorded in each provenance sidecar; that this proxy failed intermittently with server-side OSS errors (InvalidAccessKeyId on the proxy's own storage); and that the CandleCharts contest page was cited from the project brief and a search result but not fully retrieved. Its evidence is therefore genuine but brokered, and it says so.

Simulation only and explicitly not affiliated with or endorsed by Kalshi; no API key exists in the project and no order is ever submitted. Third-party claims such as Reddit backtest posts may enter only as discovery-only inputs, never as price sources — the forward ledger is the test. data/site/verification.json also names this directory's sister entry 'Commodities — Kalshi Research Exchange' as a related project referenced line by line for the exchange's mechanics.
